subject: FinPay: downstream pipeline latency spike — triage, product asks, and customer note
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] FinPay p99 latency spike — preliminary triage

Team,

Alert fired at 08:05 PDT: FinPay (account id 45123) is seeing a p99 tail latency surge from ~380ms to ~1.6s for downstream reranking calls. Error rates are stable (<=0.1%), but token-generation latencies for multi-turn flows are elevated.

What we've observed (initial):
- Spike began ~07:55 PDT, coincident with a routing config change we pushed at 07:40 (per Jonas' rollout).
- KV cache hit rate for the affected fleet dropped from 92% -> 54% over 10 minutes.
- Affected models: rwd-mistral-16k-v1 (serving variant).

Immediate mitigation executed:
- Rolled back the routing tweak for the affected pool (07:58).
- Enabled emergency increased cache retention (temporary config) on nodes serving FinPay traffic.

Next steps I'm running now: full cache snapshot, heap/CPU check, and correlate with the routing map. I attached initial logs (finpay_latency_logs_0914.zip) and kv cache snapshot.

No customer-facing message yet — we should coordinate. Marcus

Thanks Marcus — clear summary.

A few coordination asks from product/ops:
1) Customer note: Tessa, can you draft an external-facing one-paragraph acknowledgement (+ ETA) that we can send to FinPay? Goal: reassure, include mitigations we ran, and promise a technical follow-up within 24 hours.
2) Roadmap asks: if this is related to cache evaporation caused by routing changes, we need short/medium term asks:
   - Short: safe rollback guardrails and a preflight cache-heat check for routing pushes (owner: Jonas)
   - Medium: QoS-aware routing to avoid evicting hot keys for high-SLA customers, and better per-account cache quotas (owner: Product/Infra)
3) Impact classification: raise this for SLA exception review (Marissa), we may need to offer SLA credit if customer reports business impact.

Marcus, please include the confidence level on root cause and any repro steps. Jonas, what did the rollout change at 07:40 touch exactly?

I'll assemble an exec note after Tessa's draft. Please keep replies short — we need to consolidate for the customer and leadership.

Irene

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] FinPay p99 latency spike — preliminary triage

Quick technical addendum and confidence:  
- Confidence: medium-high that the root cause was a routing change that increased shard diversification for FinPay traffic, which caused their working set to be split across more nodes and exposed cold KV cache entries (evictions). No model code change.
- Evidence: KV eviction counters spiking + increased cache-miss latency correlated with drop in hit rate we saw. Node CPU/mem stable.
- Repro steps: emulate traffic with same session affinity distribution (I ran a small replay using the last 30 minutes of FinPay requests and reproduced p99 >1s when routing mode=diverse).

Mitigations we applied: rollback routing, increased cache retention, temporary per-account cache bump for FinPay. Early telemetry shows p99 returning toward baseline (~420ms) but still noisy.

Next:
- I will run a full replay and provide a 2-hour timeline with before/after graphs.
- Jonas: please attach the rollout change diff (what switches were flipped at 07:40).
- Ops: we should add a preflight check that computes projected cache-eviction delta for any routing change affecting accounts with >X qps.

I'll push full logs to Confluence runbook and link here when done. Marcus

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay service note: elevated latency this morning (08:00 PDT)

Alex —

Quick update from Redwood: we observed elevated generation latencies affecting a subset of your multi-turn flows starting ~08:00 PDT this morning. We detected the issue quickly and performed rollback and cache adjustments; our initial telemetry shows latencies trending back towards normal.

What we did:
- Rolled back a routing change that impacted how your traffic was distributed.
- Temporarily increased cache retention for your sessions and added a per-account cache boost.
- Monitoring is continuous; no increase in error rates was seen.

What it means for you:
- Short-term: you may have seen slower responses for a small percentage of requests between 08:00–08:15 PDT. We do not see request failures tied to the event.
- Recommended action: if you can avoid very long contexts or extremely bursty test runs for the next 2 hours, that will help us validate the fix more quickly.

Next update: we will send a technical follow-up within 4 hours with root cause and remediation, and a committed postmortem within 72 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously. Please reply here if you saw any direct business impact and we'll escalate.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Consolidated actions, product asks, and SLA review (FinPay latency spike)

Team / Alex —

Thanks for the quick turnaround yesterday. This note consolidates owners, asks, and the product/roadmap decisions we need to track off the incident.

Summary: rollback + cache bump restored p99 toward baseline; root cause is routing-induced cache fragmentation (medium-high confidence). No customer-requested credit yet.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: complete replay analysis and send before/after graphs + exact repro steps (ETA: 2026-09-15 14:00 PDT).
- Jonas: attach rollout diff and add a preflight check for cache-eviction projection to the routing deploy checklist (ETA: 2026-09-17).
- Product/Infra (Irene): scope QoS-aware routing and per-account cache quotas as a roadmap ticket — need rough effort estimate and priority (ETA: initial estimate by 2026-09-22).
- Marissa: review SLA impact and advise on whether to offer a formal credit if FinPay reports business loss (ETA: 2026-09-16).
- Tessa: send a short technical follow-up to FinPay with telemetry and planned timeline for the postmortem (you already sent the initial). Please include the ask to avoid heavy burst tests for 2 hours yesterday to help validation.

Customer comms cadence: initial ack (sent), technical follow-up (Tessa, within 4h of initial), postmortem (full, within 72h). Alex — please flag here if the incident led to measurable business impact; we'll prioritize SLA remediation accordingly.

Product asks / roadmap framing: this incident highlights a cross-cutting need: routing changes must be paired with a predictive cache-eviction estimate and a per-account safety cap. I'll open a roadmap ticket and propose a phased approach: 1) deploy preflight checks, 2) conservative QoS routing, 3) longer-term cache quotas + dynamic warming.

Please keep thread updates concise; I'll prepare an exec summary for Leadership once Marcus attaches the graphs.

Irene Choi
Product Lead, Inference
Redwood Inference
